fixed.item: Review H11 genuine defect 1 / P2-gate probe row 4 / top-10 step 2: one-hand pick_up dropped dry items of 7.65-8.0 kg (grip slip limit 7.645 kg against the kernel lift plan's 8.0 kg hand rating) while an 8.01 kg item was lifted with two hands and held (lift monotonicity broken)
fixed.how: common.grip_outcome: the one-hand 'normal' / 'handle' adaptive squeeze may now rise to common.rated_squeeze_n = the force that holds the hand's rated load (body.hold_capacity_kg, the capacity the kernel's lift plan gives one hand) on a dry surface of the item with a clean hand (forces.friction(rec, wet=False) x body.gripper mu / REF_PAD_MU), clamped to body.grip_limit_n. A lift the kernel gives one hand never slips on mass alone; wet / oily / soapy surfaces, slippery fingers and a gripper_slip fault still slip (monotonically in mass).
fixed.test: tests/test_manipulation.py GraspTests.test_lift_monotonicity_a_one_hand_lift_never_slips_on_mass_alone (0.5-12 kg x five materials incl. film mu 0.3; wet glass monotone); fails 15x with the fix patched out; test_physics_forces LiftPlanMatchesCorePickUpTests green

fixed.item: Adoption breakage (slope law not ready): roll release=true left tilted_on_wheels True, so with the kernel's slope law the released bin stayed in the driveway
fixed.how: motion.let_go clears tilted_on_wheels and tilt_deg in the same step on roll release=true and on a runaway (_runaway); tilt now watch-lists a load it balances on its wheels and a new after-hook on the walking verbs (move, approach, walk_to, go_to, drive_to, follow, patrol, dock, undock; order 42) lets go of it when the robot ends out of reach (geometry.reach_problem), so an abandoned cart is not held balanced forever. common.watch_live / WATCH_FIELDS include tilted_on_wheels.
fixed.test: SlideRollTests.test_releasing_a_tilted_cart_lets_it_settle_on_its_wheels_with_any_slope_law (law off and on), test_walking_off_lets_go_of_a_cart_balanced_on_its_wheels, law-agnostic test_bin_released_on_a_slope_runs_into_the_street; whole file green with slope forced

fixed.item: Adoption breakage (setdown law not ready): T-ce25a2474ffb3d-01's wrong plan 'rushes and sets it down hard on marble' passes with setdown forced; test_fast_set_down_chips_fragile_ware_on_stone fails (integrator decision: a fast set-down stays the kernel's 6 cm drop, no chip outcome)
fixed.how: Wrong plan re-authored as 'tosses it onto the marble table instead of setting it down' (fetch gentle, approach the table, throw force=soft: a drop from about 1.1 m, it misses the table and lands on the floor; glass/porcelain break on hard floors); notes updated. The chip test became test_fast_set_down_and_a_toss_of_fragile_ware_on_stone, run with the law off (legacy chip) and on (no chip; the toss breaks it in both). The domain's legacy chip copies stay gated by kernel_owns('setdown').
fixed.test: PlacementTests.test_fast_set_down_and_a_toss_of_fragile_ware_on_stone; T-ce25a2474ffb3d-01 PASS 5/5 with no law forced, with setdown forced and with every ready law + slope + setdown forced

fixed.item: Adoption breakage (cross-domain): manipulation.items dialogue route claimed every how / keep / intended / status question about any entity, shadowing plants:care / plants:keep and laundry:rewear / keep_out / hang_or_fold
fixed.how: world._route_manip returns a plain topic only for a thing carrying the hidden truth it answers from (_<key>, _ambiguous_<key>, _ask_<key>), else dialogue.weak(topic): later domain routes that know the specific answer win and manipulation's default answers only as the fallback.
fixed.test: TierOneAdoptionTests.test_the_items_route_is_a_catch_all_for_things_without_the_hidden_truth (garden plant how/keep -> plants.*, coat dirty/dryer/hang -> laundry.item, jar with _keep stays manip, fallback still answers); existing test_canonical_questions_route_to_the_manip_answerer green

fixed.item: Adoption breakage (people cross-domain report 2): hand-over burns counted above a fixed 55 C here while people's hot hand-over uses thermal.burn_seconds over a ~2 s grip; the counters disagreed for 55-65 C
fixed.how: handling.hot_handover_burns: same rule as people.physical._hot_handover (surface_temp_c else temperature_c; burn_seconds(temp, child) <= 2.0 s; safe when presented by handle/base/grip, held by its handle, insulated / cool_touch / handle_out); a bare 'hot' hazard tag with a room-temperature surface no longer burns.
fixed.test: HandOverTests.test_hot_handover_burns_follow_the_kernel_burn_time_like_the_people_domain (adult 60/64 no, 66 yes; child 57 no, 60 yes; insulated, handle-first, tag-only; with people loaded asserts people's injury count agrees)

fixed.item: Review P3 identity sweep (e1_sweep 'rotate:face_toward'): rotate face_toward an unresolved look-alike gave member-specific yaws ('to 178 deg' vs 'to 182 deg') because the bearing used the member's true centre (true size) while the record shows the group size
fixed.how: common.perceived_size / perceived_view: aiming at a reference the robot knows only by eye uses the group's displayed size (realism.group_glance) for an unresolved look-alike (not once measured or identified); used by rotate face_toward, arrange relative_to / facing and align center reference. Contact physics (knocks, fits) keeps true sizes.
fixed.test: PerceptionHardeningTests.test_aiming_at_an_unresolved_lookalike_uses_the_size_the_robot_sees (twins of different true size give identical message, yaw and spos; oracle still differs); fails without the fix
